sections.h2: Where is Berkeley County, SC, and how big is it?
sections.html:
Berkeley County sits north of Charleston County in the Lowcountry and covers 1,233.88 square miles, of which 130.26 are water, about 10.6 percent. It touches Georgetown, Williamsburg, Clarendon, Orangeburg, Dorchester and Charleston counties, and it is part of the Charleston metropolitan area.

Much of the land is protected or wet. The county lists the Bonneau Ferry, Canal, Hatchery, Moultrie Hunt Unit and Wee Tee wildlife management areas, plus Cypress Gardens and Old Santee Canal Park. A seller with acreage near those areas has a different property than a seller in a Goose Creek subdivision, and the tax class can differ too.

sections.h2: What is the history of Berkeley County?
sections.html:
The county was established in 1682 and named for John and William Berkeley, co-owners of the Province of Carolina. It became part of the Charleston District in 1769, and the current county was re-established in 1882 with its seat at Mount Pleasant. The seat moved to Moncks Corner in 1895.

The Old Berkeley County Courthouse was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1971. The Auditor and Real Property offices both list their address at 1003 Highway 52 in Moncks Corner.

sections.h2: How fast is Berkeley County growing?
sections.html:
The 2020 Census counted 229,861 residents, up 29.2 percent from 177,843 in 2010. A 2025 estimate is 274,666. There were 85,539 households and 93,623 housing units in 2020, and the median age was 36.6.

Goose Creek is the largest community and Moncks Corner is the county seat. Hanahan is in the county, and Summerville is partly in Berkeley, Dorchester and Charleston counties. Other named places include Ladson, Bonneau, Jamestown, St. Stephen, Pinopolis and Sangaree. About 77.9 percent of residents live in urban areas.

The county's real property office says it values more than 110,000 properties, which gives a sense of how many parcels the county has to bill every October.

sections.h2: What jobs and employers shape Berkeley County?
sections.html:
Manufacturing is the largest sector at 9,406 jobs, or 15.8 percent, followed by retail trade, accommodation and food services, and professional and technical services. Total employment was 59,417, with an average annual wage of $62,118 and unemployment around 3 percent from 2022 through 2024.

Named major employers include Blackbaud, Booz Allen Hamilton, Nucor, Publix, Volvo Cars and Walmart. The 2022 gross domestic product was $10.6 billion.

sections.h2: Who bills and collects property tax in Berkeley County?
sections.html:
The Auditor's Office publishes the due dates and takes business personal property returns, the Treasurer collects and disburses the money, and the Real Property Services office values the land and buildings. The county says the Treasurer collects real, personal and motor vehicle taxes and pays out funds to the county, municipalities, schools and special taxing districts.

  • Auditor: 1003 Highway 52, Moncks Corner 29461, (843) 719-4309.
  • Real Property Services: (843) 719-4061, at the same administration building.
  • Online payments: the county's payments site charges a PayPal convenience fee that the county does not receive.

Real estate is billed in arrears, with bills mailed in October and due the following January 15. If a due date lands on a weekend or holiday, it moves to the next business day, and a mailed payment must carry a postmark on or before the due date.

sections.h2: What are the penalties if Berkeley County taxes are late?
sections.html:
Late payments start picking up penalties on January 16, and under state law the charges are 3 percent, then 7 percent more from February 2, then 5 percent more from March 17. Once that last date passes, the treasurer can issue an execution for the taxes, penalties and costs.

The county's Delinquent Tax Department says a bill is delinquent after March 16 and then goes to that office. It sends certified notices with restricted delivery, and it plans and runs land and mobile home sales, advertised in the Post and Courier. After a sale it also handles title research and the deed.

If title changed during the tax year and the new owner got no timely notice, state law tells the treasurer to waive the penalties.

sections.h2: How does reassessment work in Berkeley County?
sections.html:
The county page says state law requires reassessment of all property every five years, and it lists 1981, 1985, 1999, 2004, 2009, 2014, 2019 and 2024 as program years. Properties are appraised at fair market value, and millage is set by dividing each taxing entity's budget by the assessments.

The Real Property office processes appeals of its values and represents the county before the Board of Assessment Appeals and the South Carolina Administrative Law Court. State law gives you 90 days from the notice mailing to file a written objection, then 30 days after the assessor's response to go to the board.

  • An objection in writing should name the value or ratio you dispute.
  • A conference is scheduled within about 30 days of a meeting request.
  • A board decision can be taken to the Administrative Law Court within 30 days.

Call the office to confirm which program year applies to your parcel and what your notice says.

sections.h2: How does a sale affect the 4 percent rate in Berkeley County?
sections.html:
The 4 percent legal residence rate is not automatic, and Berkeley County asks buyers and deed changers to apply. In its January 2024 notice the Real Property Department said applications were open to recent buyers who will live in the home, and to owners who added or removed a name, created a life estate or trust, or lost an owner. The deadline that year was January 15.

Existing recipients do not need to reapply unless their circumstances change, and the breakdown appears on the yearly tax bill. The office also reviews agricultural use, rollback taxes, builder and HOA classifications, and a Commercial ATI exemption.

When you sell, expect the buyer to start a new application. A home without the 4 percent rate is taxed at 6 percent under state law.

sections.h2: Selling a Berkeley County house with tax due
sections.html:
You can sell the house and have the closing agent pay the taxes from the proceeds, instead of waiting for a delinquent sale. If a sale already happened, the owner, a grantee, or a mortgage or judgment creditor can redeem within twelve months, with interest on the bid that rises from 3 percent in the first quarter to 12 percent in the fourth.

Cash Home Buyers purchases houses in Berkeley County as they are, including inherited and tenant-occupied ones. Share the address, the latest tax notice and your timeline, and we will respond with a straight answer.

faqs.q: When are Berkeley County, SC property taxes due?
faqs.a: January 15 of the year after the October billing. Mailed payments need a postmark on or before the due date, and a weekend due date moves to the next business day.

faqs.q: Where is the Berkeley County Auditor's office?
faqs.a: The Auditor is at 1003 Highway 52, Moncks Corner, SC 29461, and the phone is (843) 719-4309. Real Property Services can be reached at (843) 719-4061.

faqs.q: How do I get the 4 percent rate on a Berkeley County home?
faqs.a: Apply with Berkeley County Real Property after you buy a home you will live in. The county's January 2024 notice set a January 15 deadline and said recipients do not reapply unless things change.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal a Berkeley County value?
faqs.a: State law gives 90 days from the date the assessor mails a notice to file a written objection. After the assessor responds you have 30 days to appeal to the board.

faqs.q: What are the late penalties in Berkeley County?
faqs.a: State law adds 3 percent after the due date, 7 percent more from February 2, and 5 percent more from March 17. After that the bill goes to execution and the Delinquent Tax Department.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Berkeley County house that has delinquent tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The unpaid taxes, penalties and costs can be paid from the sale proceeds at closing. Ask the county for a payoff figure that matches your closing date.
